title: Affine supported perfect zero detector
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], equipped with derived localizations for its module sheaves and their open restrictions [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $s$ be a finite set of affine opens covering $X$ with $|s|\leq 1$. Let $T\subseteq X$ be closed with quasi-compact complement. There exists a perfect quasi-coherent derived object $E$ [def-pc-perfect-complex] whose cohomology stalks vanish outside $T$, such that, for every quasi-coherent derived object $K$ supported on $T$, vanishing of $\operatorname{Hom}(E[n],K)$ for all $n\in\mathbf Z$ implies that $K$ is zero.

proof.text: The cardinality bound makes the finite cover either empty or a singleton. In the singleton case its member equals top by the cover equality. In the empty case bottom equals top. Both opens are affine, so the top subscheme, hence X, is affine.

Set U=X minus T and apply the affine Koszul construction and open-unit comparison to obtain a perfect supported quasi-coherent E, a right adjoint R to derived restriction, and an adjunction whose unit at every quasi-coherent K orthogonal to the shifts of E is invertible.

For a supported K orthogonal to E, derived restriction is zero by the stalkwise restriction-vanishing lemma. The adjunction identifies every endomorphism of R(K restricted to U) with a map into the zero restriction. These maps are all equal, so its identity equals zero and the pushforward is zero. Transport the zero-object property across the invertible unit.

proof_origin.note: The source route is unchanged; affine-cover reduction, supported restriction vanishing, and right-adjoint zero preservation are implemented in Lean.

No equivalent statement. For triangulated closure the source has DerivedCategory.homologyProperty_isTriangulated, which additionally needs weak Serre class instances; these are not supplied for the supported quasi-coherent property. Existing KoszulOpenOrthogonality supplies the orthogonality input, not the finite supported perfect object construction. PerfectGenerationOpenInduction concerns all quasi-coherent objects rather than a supported category.

lean.statement:
theorem supported_perfect_detector_affine
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (s : Finset X.affineOpens) (hcover : (⨆ U ∈ s, (U : X.Opens)) = ⊤)
    (hcard : s.card ≤ 1) (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ) :
    ∃ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X, Scheme.IsPerfect X E.obj ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T →
        Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj E.obj).val.presheaf x))) ∧
      ∀ K : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X,
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T →
          Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj K.obj).val.presheaf x))) →
        (∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (E.obj⟦n⟧ ⟶ K.obj)) → IsZero K.obj
